messages:
noah: quick note — onboarding qwen-bridge variant, weird head-swap pattern on long context tests
tara: describe, please: is this on export or runtime load?
noah: export writes head order as [0..31] but runtime expects a permuted ordering for some fused kernels, only triggers after token ~900
lin: did you verify tokenizer mapping? any diacritic/ZWJ remap?
noah: tokenizer preserved. converter made an internal "alias" mapping for soft hyphen and a few combining diacritics (12 ids)
miles: soft hyphen remaps have bitten us before. int4 tends to amplify marginal embedding shifts
noah: interestingly, this repros in fp16 too — but int4/int8 make it show earlier and more extreme
tara: sounds like two orthogonal issues: head-order handshake + subtle embedding shadowing. need to isolate
lin: proposal: 1) convert with --remap-vocab=preserve 2) force --head-order=strict and add metadata header layout=splithead 3) run fp16 vs int8 vs int4 sweeps
noah: also add a repeat-prefix KV warmup test (repeat 5x) and log per-head attention entropy
ci-bot: CI queued: onboard/qwen-bridge-headswap #204. Artifacts will be at /artifacts/1839998888 in ~25m
miles: if head-order is the culprit, we can detect mismatch by computing cosine between param blocks and expected ordering and auto-flip on load
tara: and if vocab shadowing correlates with drift, add a post-convert token-alignment map to the artifacts so we can diff quickly
noah: running conversions now: strict remap + head-order explicit + fp16/int8/int4 short evals. will upload diffs
lin: add unit test with combined diacritics + ZWJ + soft-hyphen sequences — minimal failing case helps triage
noah: filed ONB-5090 with steps, linked artifacts, and short rouge/table. will update when CI done
miles: thanks. if the rotary phase sweep helps, we can set converter defaults per-model family and document it in the catalog
noah: noted, will include rotary-scale sweep 0.8->1.1 step 0.05 in the run
tara: ping us when artifacts ready. we should avoid making int4 default until canary passes
noah: will do — thanks all
